10.1.simple: Krishna speaks again to Arjuna, calling him dear and saying he shares this for Arjuna's good. Real teaching comes from care for the listener.

10.2.simple: Not even gods or great sages fully know where Krishna comes from, because he is the source of them all. The deepest reality is bigger than any mind that tries to grasp it.

10.3.simple: Whoever understands the Divine as unborn, without beginning, and Lord of all worlds sees clearly and is freed from wrongdoing. Knowing the true source changes how we live.

10.4.simple: Krishna begins a list of human qualities: understanding, wisdom, clear thinking, forgiveness, truthfulness, self-control, calm, joy and sorrow, birth and death, fear and courage. All of our inner life has one source.

10.5.simple: The list continues: non-violence, balance, contentment, discipline, generosity, fame and disgrace. All these varied states of beings arise from Krishna. Even our inner states are part of a larger whole.

10.6.simple: The great sages and ancient founders of humanity, Krishna says, were born from his mind, and all beings descend from them. Every generation traces back to one source.

10.7.simple: Whoever truly grasps Krishna's many expressions and his power becomes steady and unshakeable in spirit. Seeing the Divine behind the world brings deep stability.

10.8.simple: Krishna says he is the source of everything and all things come forth from him. Wise people who understand this turn to him with heartfelt love.

10.9.simple: Those whose thoughts and lives are centred on the Divine love to talk about it with one another, sharing insights and finding joy and contentment together. Spiritual friendship lifts everyone.

10.10.simple: To those who stay devoted with love, Krishna gives clear understanding (inner wisdom to see what matters), which guides them to him. Love opens the way to wisdom.

10.11.simple: Out of pure compassion, Krishna, living within each heart, lights a lamp of knowledge that removes the darkness of ignorance. Inner clarity is a gift of grace.

10.12.simple: Arjuna responds with wonder, naming Krishna as the highest reality, the supreme home, the purifier, eternal, divine, the first God, unborn and everywhere.

10.13.simple: Arjuna notes that great sages like Narada, Asita, Devala and Vyasa have all said this, and now Krishna himself confirms it. Tradition and personal experience meet.

10.14.simple: Arjuna says he accepts everything Krishna has told him as true, and admits that neither gods nor demons fully understand Krishna's nature. It is humble, trusting acceptance.

10.15.simple: Only Krishna truly knows himself, Arjuna says, calling him source of all beings, God of gods and Lord of the world. The infinite can only be fully known from within.

10.16.simple: Arjuna asks Krishna to describe fully the divine glories through which he fills all worlds. He wants to see how the Divine shows up in everything.

10.17.simple: Arjuna asks a practical question: how can I keep you in mind, and in which things should I think of you? He wants a way to remember the sacred in daily life.

10.18.simple: Arjuna asks to hear again, in detail, about Krishna's power and glory, saying he can never get enough of these life-giving words. True wisdom never feels like too much.

10.19.simple: Krishna agrees to name his most prominent glories, but says there is no end to them in detail. The list that follows is a sample, not a complete catalogue.

10.20.simple: Krishna first says he is the Self living in the heart of every being, and their beginning, middle and end. Before any outward glory, the sacred lives within everyone.

10.21.simple: Among bright and powerful things Krishna names the best: Vishnu among the sun gods, the sun among lights, the moon among stars. Wherever you see radiance, think of the Divine.

10.22.simple: Krishna is the musical Sama Veda, the king of the gods, the mind among the senses and consciousness in living beings. Awareness itself points to the sacred.

10.23.simple: Among powerful beings Krishna names Shiva, Kubera the lord of wealth, fire, and Mount Meru. The greatest in each group points beyond itself to the Divine.

10.24.simple: Krishna is Brihaspati, chief of priests, Skanda, chief of generals, and the ocean among waters. In leadership, strength and vastness, we can glimpse the sacred.

10.25.simple: Krishna is Bhrigu among sages, Om among sounds, quiet repetition of a sacred word among offerings, and the Himalayas among mountains. Stillness and steadiness reveal the Divine.

10.26.simple: Krishna is the sacred peepul (fig) tree, the sage Narada, the celestial musician Chitraratha and the sage Kapila. Wisdom, music and the living tree all carry his presence.

10.27.simple: Among horses and elephants Krishna names the legendary royal ones, and among people, the king. Excellence and noble leadership point to the sacred.

10.28.simple: Krishna is the thunderbolt among weapons, the wish-fulfilling cow, the power of love that brings new life, and the serpent king Vasuki. Power used for life reflects the Divine.

10.29.simple: Krishna names himself as the great serpent Ananta, Varuna lord of waters, the chief of ancestors, and Yama who keeps order. Even guardians of justice and endings reflect him.

10.30.simple: Krishna is Prahlada, the devoted boy born among demons; time among all that measures; the lion among animals; and Garuda among birds. Goodness can shine even in unlikely places.

10.31.simple: Krishna is the wind that purifies, Rama among warriors, the mightiest of sea creatures and the river Ganga. Cleansing, courage and life-giving flow all reflect him.

10.32.simple: Krishna is the beginning, middle and end of all creation, the knowledge of the Self among sciences, and honest reasoning in debate. The search for truth itself is sacred.

10.33.simple: Krishna is the first letter 'A', the simplest joining of words, endless time and the one who gives each action its result. He is in the building blocks of language and life.

10.34.simple: Krishna is death that takes all and the source of everything yet to be born. He also names qualities like fame, beauty, speech, memory, intelligence, steadiness and patience.

10.35.simple: Krishna is the finest hymn, the Gayatri rhythm, the best month and spring, the season of flowers. Beauty and freshness in time and nature carry the Divine.

10.36.simple: Krishna is even the cleverness of the gambler, the brilliance of the brilliant, victory, determination and the goodness of good people. Every kind of ability draws on one source, so the call is to use it well.

10.37.simple: Krishna names himself among his own family, among the Pandavas as Arjuna himself, among sages as Vyasa, and among poets as Ushana. Arjuna learns he too reflects the Divine.

10.38.simple: Krishna is the authority that keeps order, wise strategy in those who seek success, silence among secrets and wisdom in the wise. Quiet, wise strength reflects him.

10.39.simple: Krishna says he is the seed of all beings; nothing, moving or still, could exist without him. He is the root of everything that lives.

10.40.simple: There is no end to Krishna's divine glories; what he has shared is only a small sample. The sacred is endless, always more than we can list.

10.41.simple: Wherever you find anything glorious, beautiful or powerful, know that it springs from a spark of Krishna's splendour. This is the key to the whole chapter.

10.42.simple: Krishna ends: why worry over all these details? With just one small part of himself he supports the entire universe. The point is not the list, but the awe it awakens.

lessons.title: Every quality has one source
lessons.teaching: Krishna says even the gods cannot fully grasp where he comes from, because he is the source of all. Our understanding, forgiveness, calm, courage, joy and sorrow all arise from that one source. Seeing this helps us hold our inner life with less ego and more gratitude.
lessons.keyIdea: Your best qualities are gifts flowing from one source.

apply.scenario: Your coach praises your calm under pressure in a big match. You feel tempted to brag that you are simply better than your teammates.
apply.question: What would the Gita suggest?
options: Brag a little; you earned it.
Downplay it and insist you were just lucky.
Accept the praise with gratitude, seeing calm and skill as gifts that come from a deeper source.
Change the subject so nobody notices you.
apply.why: In 10.4-10.5 Krishna says qualities like intelligence, self-control and calm arise from him alone, so gratitude fits better than pride.

lessons.reflect: Which of your strengths could you hold as a gift rather than a trophy?
lessons.practice: Thank someone or something for a quality you have that you did not create alone.

lessons.title: Wisdom grows in good company
lessons.teaching: Those who see the Divine as the source of everything find joy in talking about it with each other, lighting up each other's understanding. To those who stay steady in love, Krishna gives the inner wisdom to find their way.
lessons.keyIdea: Share what inspires you; wisdom grows when it is shared.

apply.scenario: You have found a book that is changing how you see life. Your study group mostly talks about gossip and grades.
apply.question: What would the Gita suggest?
options: Gently share what you are learning and seek out friends who enjoy such conversations too.
Keep it to yourself; people will think you are weird.
Lecture your group until they agree it is important.
Quit the study group since they are not deep enough.
apply.why: In 10.9 Krishna describes devoted people enlightening one another and finding joy in speaking of the Divine together.

lessons.reflect: Who in your life helps you see more clearly, and do you tell them?
lessons.practice: Share one inspiring idea with a friend today and ask what inspires them.

lessons.title: A lamp lit from within
lessons.teaching: Out of compassion, Krishna lights a lamp of knowledge in the heart that clears away confusion. Arjuna responds with humble trust and asks to understand more. Clarity often comes when we are open and keep asking honestly.
lessons.keyIdea: Light one lamp of understanding and the darkness begins to lift.

apply.scenario: You have felt confused for weeks about which college major to pick. Everyone gives different advice and your mind feels foggy.
apply.question: What would the Gita suggest?
options: Pick at random just to end the stress.
Let your parents decide so it is not your responsibility.
Ignore the question until the deadline forces you.
Get quiet, ask honestly, and trust that clarity can arise from within as you stay open.
apply.why: In 10.11 Krishna says that, dwelling within the heart, he destroys the darkness of ignorance with the shining lamp of knowledge.

lessons.reflect: What question are you ready to ask more honestly, instead of rushing to an answer?
lessons.practice: Sit quietly for five minutes, hold one question in mind, and simply listen.

lessons.title: Where can I find you?
lessons.teaching: Arjuna asks a beautiful question: in which things should I think of you? Krishna starts with the heart of every being, then with whatever shines brightest, like the sun. Remembering the sacred is easier when we connect it to things we already see.
lessons.keyIdea: Begin with the heart, then see the sacred in what shines.

apply.scenario: You want to feel more spiritually connected, but your days are packed with work and kids, leaving no time for long practices.
apply.question: What would the Gita suggest?
options: Wait until retirement when you will have more time.
Use what is already around you, like sunrise or a loved one's face, as reminders of the sacred.
Force yourself into a two-hour daily routine you cannot keep.
Decide spirituality just is not for busy people.
apply.why: In 10.17 Arjuna asks in what things to think of Krishna, and in 10.20-10.21 Krishna points to the Self in every heart and the radiant sun.

lessons.reflect: What everyday sight could become your reminder of something sacred?
lessons.practice: Notice the sun or sky once today and let it remind you of the Divine.

lessons.title: Greatness in quiet things
lessons.teaching: Krishna names himself as the mind among the senses, Om among sounds, silent repetition among offerings, and the Himalayas among mountains. The sacred often shows up as steadiness, stillness and awareness, not just noise and display.
lessons.keyIdea: The Divine often speaks through stillness, steadiness and awareness.

apply.scenario: You feel pressure to post constantly online to prove your life is exciting. Your quiet morning walks feel 'too boring' to count.
apply.question: What would the Gita suggest?
options: Post more often so you do not fall behind your friends.
Skip the walks and do something more impressive.
Delete all your accounts in frustration.
Value the quiet walks; stillness and steady awareness can be among the most sacred things.
apply.why: In 10.25 Krishna names himself as the silent repetition among offerings and the unmoving Himalayas, honouring stillness and steadiness.

lessons.reflect: Where in your life does stillness feel most meaningful?
lessons.practice: Spend three minutes in silence today, without your phone, simply breathing.

lessons.title: Look for the best in each
lessons.teaching: Krishna keeps naming the finest in each group: the lion among animals, the Ganga among rivers, Rama among warriors, honest reasoning in debate. Even Prahlada, a devoted soul born among demons, shows that goodness can shine anywhere.
lessons.keyIdea: In every group, look for the best; it points to the sacred.

apply.scenario: A new colleague comes from a team everyone at work complains about. Your friends assume she will be difficult too.
apply.question: What would the Gita suggest?
options: Look for her real strengths and goodness; excellence can appear anywhere.
Keep your distance just to be safe.
Go along with the group's opinion to fit in.
Test her with a hard task to see if she fails.
apply.why: In 10.30 Krishna names himself as Prahlada among the demons, a reminder that goodness can shine even where we least expect it.

lessons.reflect: Who have you judged by their group rather than by who they are?
lessons.practice: Find and name one genuine strength in someone you usually overlook.

lessons.title: Time, spring and resolve
lessons.teaching: Krishna is endless time, the season of flowers, determination in the resolute and goodness in the good. Every ability, even cleverness, has one source, so the real question is how we use our gifts. Arjuna himself is named among the glories.
lessons.keyIdea: Every gift comes from one source; use yours for good.

apply.scenario: You are naturally persuasive. A classmate asks you to help talk the teacher into accepting work that was copied.
apply.question: What would the Gita suggest?
options: Help; being persuasive is your talent, so use it.
Stay out of it and say nothing either way.
Decline kindly and use your persuasiveness for something good, like helping them ask for an extension honestly.
Report them immediately without talking to them.
apply.why: In 10.36 Krishna names himself as resolve and the goodness of the good: our abilities flow from one source, and we are invited to use them well.

lessons.reflect: Which of your gifts could you use more intentionally for good?
lessons.practice: Use one of your talents today to help someone without being asked.

lessons.title: A spark of splendour everywhere
lessons.teaching: Krishna says his glories are endless and that whatever is beautiful, powerful or excellent is a spark of his splendour. The point is not memorising the list, but learning to feel awe wherever greatness appears.
lessons.keyIdea: Wherever you see splendour, you are glimpsing a spark of the Divine.

apply.scenario: You watch a friend play a stunning piano piece. Your first thought is envy because you could never play like that.
apply.question: What would the Gita suggest?
options: Avoid their concerts so you do not feel bad.
Point out their mistakes to feel better.
Decide you are simply untalented and stop trying music.
Let the beauty move you with wonder, seeing it as a spark of something sacred.
apply.why: In 10.41 Krishna says whatever is glorious or beautiful comes from a spark of his splendour, so awe fits better than envy.

lessons.reflect: When did you last feel genuine wonder at someone else's gift?
lessons.practice: Notice one beautiful thing today and pause long enough to feel awe.
